action_formats.fenced_file: One fenced code block containing the whole replacement file.
action_formats.format_failure: Any sample that is none of the three accepted formats. Counted by format_failure_rate and not folded into the correctness reward.
action_formats.json_tool_call: A <tool_call>{...}</tool_call> object, as in scripts/run_local_agent.py, or one JSON object whose name is apply_patch.
action_formats.unified_diff: A unified diff, fenced or bare, with a diff --git line or ---, +++, and @@ headers.

evaluation_identical_across_arms.target_heldout_tasks: 15-20, chosen only after the 20-30 task expansion

changes_from_v1: mlsys-v1-causal-attention is excluded from any future held-out set. It and train row_log_softmax are the same stable-softmax repair, and the prompts both call out large finite values. The v1 split file is unchanged. The three utilities under benchmarks/mlsys_coding_v2 are unassigned pool candidates. They are not a held-out set.
Held-out membership is not frozen. The target is 15-20 tasks drawn from a 20-30 task pool (step 3). The current v1 held-out pool has 4 tasks. Membership will be frozen by hash before any training.

The primary test is a task-level one-sided paired t-test at alpha 0.05 for GRPO versus no-update and for SFT versus no-update, with a Holm correction across those two contrasts. A task-clustered bootstrap confidence interval is secondary and is not an acceptance gate. v1 required every seed difference to be positive.
The training screen is pass@8 at temperature 1 on the train split, and it comes before the held-out test. The power model is invalid near 0% success. format_failure_rate is a separate metric.
Accepted model actions are a JSON tool call, a fenced whole file, or a unified diff.

cost_sketch.note: The 12.29 tokens/s figure is the retained CPU code-repair feasibility rate on a different task that scored 0/32. It is not a measurement of this pack. Trained-arm attempts are tasks times 3 seeds times k=32. No-update attempts are tasks times k=32 once, matching the power script. These sketches describe the unfrozen target. They were not run. In the power table, raising k from 8 to 32 moves the single-test minimum detectable effect more than adding the next block of tasks (10 tasks at k=32 is 8.5 points; 20 tasks at k=8 is 12 points). The retained OpenBookQA 0.5B CPU training peak was 11924.6 MiB, above the 8 GiB cap.

metrics.acceptance: For each pre-specified primary contrast, form the per-task difference of mean protocol success and run a one-sided paired t-test. Apply Holm step-down across the two contrasts at family-wise alpha 0.05. A contrast is accepted only when Holm rejects its p-value. The task-clustered bootstrap interval is reported and does not accept or reject.
metrics.holm: Two contrasts. Order the one-sided p-values. The smaller must be at most 0.025. The larger is tested at 0.05 only if the smaller was rejected.
metrics.per_task_statistic: No-update success rate from k samples on that task, minus the mean of the per-seed trained success rates. Each training seed contributes k samples. Success is the frozen 0/1 gate, not the shaped reward. k is 32 in the design target.
metrics.primary_statistic: One-sided paired t-test on the per-task mean differences. GRPO is the RL arm.
secondary: task-clustered bootstrap percentile interval for the mean per-task difference, report only
mean shaped protocol reward on the held-out tasks
format_failure_rate on the train screen and on the held-out attempts

power.analysis_assumption: Task logits are normal with mean -0.85 and scale 1.5, so the simulated held-out mean success is about 35%. Each training seed adds a shared logit effect plus N(0, 0.3^2) jitter. Rates are binomial proportions. This is not a measured agent success rate. The model is invalid near 0% success because of a floor effect.
power.floor_effect: The percentage-point minimum detectable effects are computed around a 35% mean. They do not apply when success is near 0. That is why the pass@8 train gate has to pass before this held-out test is interpretable.
power.holm_adjusted_mde: not recomputed. The table is one one-sided test at alpha 0.05. Holm across the two primary contrasts is more conservative: the smaller p-value must be at most 0.025.

parameters.k_definition: Binomial draws per task for the no-update rate, and binomial draws per task per training seed for the trained rate. The tested trained rate averages the seed rates. k is not a total across seeds.
parameters.rng: numpy Generator seed 0, consumed in script order
parameters.test: one-sided paired t on per-task differences

power.recommendation: After the pool reaches 20-30 tasks, freeze 15-20 held-out tasks and use k=32 with 3 training seeds. The single-test target minimum detectable effect is about 8 percentage points (15 tasks at k=32 is 8.5; 20 tasks at k=32 is 6.8). Raising k moves that effect more than adding tasks.

retired_task_cluster_screen.note: An earlier draft treated a task-cluster bootstrap percentile as the only acceptance clause, with 6 tasks and 8 seeds. That clause is not the decision rule. The numbers are kept so the screen is not dropped.

v1_at_baseline_0_5.definition: Exact P(Bin(4, arm) > Bin(4, 0.5))^3. The v1 acceptance rule is that all three seed differences are strictly positive. Under that rule the seed-bootstrap 2.5 percentile is positive whenever the rule accepts, so the bootstrap adds no rejection. This is an analysis assumption, not a measured agent rate.

reason: v1 stays in place and is not re-run. Held-out causal_attention and train row_log_softmax are the same stable-softmax repair; the train prompt says large positive and large negative rows, and the held-out prompt says finite behavior on large scores. With 4 held-out tasks, 3 seeds, and the rule that every seed improves, exact power at a baseline pass probability of 0.5 reaches 0.80 only at an absolute lift of 0.491. Under temperature 0 those three seeds are one greedy draw: the independent-seed reading has power 0.314 on a +0.25 lift from 0.05, and the greedy reading has power 0.680. The draft decision rule is a task-level paired t-test with Holm across GRPO versus no-update and SFT versus no-update. A task-clustered bootstrap interval is secondary. The power script puts the single-test 80% minimum detectable effect near 8 percentage points for 15-20 tasks at 32 samples, around a 35% mean success rate. That calculation does not apply near 0% success, so the pass@8 train gate comes first. The current held-out pool has 4 tasks, so the 15-20 task set waits on the 20-30 task expansion and is not frozen here.

training_gate.context: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct was reported at 0/5 greedy on the five train tasks because every attempt failed the tool-call format. This draft records that report as the reason to change the screen. It does not re-run the screen and it is not a new measurement.
training_gate.format_failure_rate: Fraction of samples that classify as format_failure. Recorded on its own. A format failure is not a correct sample.
training_gate.open_review_point: The gate requires at least two train tasks with a correct sample and, separately, nonzero reward variance inside at least one group of eight. Eight correct samples on a task have variance 0, so a saturated group does not by itself open the gate. A reviewer may want a hit alone to count.
training_gate.prerequisite_for_heldout_power: The paired-t power model is invalid near 0% success. The pass@8 gate has to pass before a held-out comparison under that model is interpretable.
training_gate.rule: pass@8 at temperature 1: at least 2 of 5 train tasks have at least one correct sample, and at least one group of 8 has nonzero within-group reward variance.
